placements.why: No strata exist yet for this repo, but the content is squarely an observatory calibration record (instrument, calibration value, verification against a named reference standard) — exactly the shape the org's own strata vocabulary names 'Calibration' for. Nothing existing to reuse, and this is a foundational organizational category (no parent required), so mint it standalone.
placements.title: instrument calibration and verification as an organizational record category
placements.frame: does this content record an instrument's calibration/verification state against a named reference standard?

placements.title: instrument trust is established by verification against a named reference standard, not by adjustment alone
placements.frame: was this instrument's calibration checked against a specific, named reference artifact, and does it hold across the full range claimed?
placements.why: src-1 narrates the calibration event and its verification against the June reference plates holding across the full observing band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument/calibration/verification facts as flat labelled fields. The specific 88.4 MHz reading and the June plates are one-time facts, but they evidence a recurring observatory theme — that an instrument's calibration is trusted only once checked against a named reference standard across its operating range — which future calibration envelopes for other instruments would keep feeding. No existing narrative structure exists to reuse, so this is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
